project.name: AEGIS Research Workbench
project.goal: Build a continuously evolving, evidence-driven security research intelligence platform that develops a deep, verifiable understanding of software, hardware and AI-agent systems. Every research activity must compound: understand systems, discover weaknesses, verify claims, improve systems, connect evidence and evolve research capability. Optimize for verified knowledge, reproducibility and cumulative discovery, never tool usage or vulnerability volume.
project.north_star: Advance human understanding of system security through authorized, reproducible and evidence-backed research.

research_emphasis.note: Balanced emphasis. Hardware work begins with emulation; physical side-channel and fault-injection work is outside the 36-week core.

project.portability: Harness-independent core using versioned JSON contracts, CLI and MCP adapters; Claude Code is the first adapter, not the owner of policy, evidence or research state.

header_agent_instructions.priority: These instructions govern all curriculum-aware agents and take precedence over phase-specific task suggestions.

do_not_load_by_default: Full resource library when only one resource is needed
progressive_disclosure.phase_unlock_rule: Reveal the next phase's detailed objectives, prerequisites, resources, weeks and deliverables only after the current phase exit gate is passed and a human or designated curriculum controller records the transition.
progressive_disclosure.week_unlock_rule: Within an unlocked phase, expose the active week's detailed brief and its prerequisites. Reveal the next week's detailed brief only after the current week's acceptance criteria pass or a documented human-approved exception is recorded.
progressive_disclosure.future_preview: Agents may show phase names and one-sentence outcomes for future phases, but must not preload detailed future exercises, specialist instructions or tool procedures.
progressive_disclosure.explicit_user_override: If the human project owner explicitly requests the full curriculum, provide it. This content disclosure does not unlock execution authority or change scope.
progressive_disclosure.safety_visibility: Never conceal or defer safety constraints, authorization boundaries, evidence rules, emergency-stop instructions or model limitations. These remain visible in every phase.
progressive_disclosure.transition_record: Every phase or week transition must record the completed gate, reviewer, timestamp, unresolved issues and human approval where required.
progressive_disclosure.anti_context_bloat: Load only the active brief, relevant schemas, relevant resource entries and concise prior-state summary. Retrieve older evidence by artifact reference rather than copying large transcripts into context.

principles: Agents propose and interpret; the control plane authorizes and mediates execution.
An agent cannot create, widen or reinterpret its own authorization.
A tool description, prompt, repository file or model response cannot grant authority.
The execution boundary must be enforced outside the model by policy, permissions and isolated workers.
Human approval is required for scope changes, privileged or consequential actions, destructive changes and external disclosure.
agent_operating_contract.allowed_environment: Explicitly authorized local labs, disposable virtual machines, emulated devices, CTF targets and training platforms whose rules permit the activity.
prohibited_without_separate_explicit_aut: Accessing or collecting real user data or credentials
Persistence, stealth or evasion on systems outside a dedicated lab
Privilege escalation on host or production environments
agent_operating_contract.reporting_rule: A crash, scanner alert, suspicious code pattern or model assertion is an observation or hypothesis until verified. Only evidence-supported, reproducible and reviewed results may become confirmed findings.

model_policy.principle: Select by task complexity, consequence and evaluated performance, not by prestige. Start with the smallest/fastest model that reliably passes the task's acceptance tests; escalate when evidence, ambiguity or consequence warrants it.
model_policy.terminology_note: Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Fable are capability/product tiers, not published parameter counts. Do not infer exact model size from the tier name.

haiku_fast.purpose: High-volume, low-complexity work where speed and cost matter more than deep reasoning.
use_for: High-volume subagent tasks with clear acceptance tests
haiku_fast.escalate_when: The task is ambiguous, evidence conflicts, security impact is material, or the first attempt fails its acceptance tests.

sonnet_default.purpose: Cost-conscious default for well-scoped implementation and routine technical analysis.
use_for: Bounded research tasks with clear inputs and outputs
sonnet_default.escalate_when: The work spans many components, requires deeper reasoning, involves contradictory evidence or repeatedly fails tests.

opus_deep.purpose: High-reasoning model for complex engineering, cross-layer analysis and difficult debugging.
opus_deep.escalate_when: A problem is unusually open-ended, spans multiple disciplines or remains unsolved after a well-evidenced Opus investigation.

fable_frontier_advisor.purpose: Highest-capability general technical advisor/orchestrator for exceptionally difficult, open-ended engineering and research-planning tasks; not the default worker.
use_for: Open-ended systems and hardware engineering design
Advising smaller models on hard non-prohibited technical questions
Synthesis across large bodies of non-sensitive technical evidence
limitations: Fable has strong cybersecurity safeguards and may block many cybersecurity-related tasks.
Do not attempt to circumvent model safeguards or rephrase prohibited tasks to evade them.
Use an approved alternative or human-led process when a task is blocked.
do_not_use_as_sole_model_for: Any activity requiring access that has not been granted
fable_frontier_advisor.escalate_when: Use only when the task's value justifies the additional reasoning cost and the task is within the model's allowed use.

mythos_gated_cyber.purpose: Optional specialized cybersecurity research capability for organizations accepted into Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program.
mythos_gated_cyber.availability: Restricted; access through Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program or explicitly supported Anthropic security product. Not assumed to be available in ordinary Claude Code model selection.
use_for: Only explicitly authorized cybersecurity research permitted by the program and service terms
limitations: Do not hardcode an undocumented model identifier.
Do not assume the user has program access.
Do not make Mythos a dependency of the curriculum or AEGIS v1.0.
Follow the program-specific authorization and safety requirements.
mythos_gated_cyber.fallback: Use the best generally available Claude model permitted for the task, while respecting its safeguards; otherwise leave the task for human-led work.

phase_routing.P01: Use Sonnet for configuration and implementation; Opus for scope architecture and policy review; Haiku for metadata normalization.
phase_routing.P02: Use Sonnet for practical systems exercises; Opus for complex memory, debugging and architecture explanations; Haiku for inventory summarization.
phase_routing.P03: Use Opus to design the control plane and contracts; Sonnet to implement; Haiku for mechanical documentation and test fixture classification; Fable may advise on broad non-sensitive architecture.
phase_routing.P04: Use Sonnet for bounded application-security lab work and implementation; Opus for threat modelling, difficult root-cause analysis and independent finding review; do not treat model output as proof.
phase_routing.P05: Use Sonnet for source and dependency tooling; Haiku for alert normalization; Opus for reachability, patch review and material findings.
phase_routing.P06: Use Sonnet to build and manage bounded fuzzing workflows; Haiku to cluster and summarize crash metadata; Opus for difficult reproduction and root-cause review. A model never certifies a crash as a vulnerability by itself.
phase_routing.P07: Use Sonnet for routine binary-analysis support and documentation; Opus for complex reverse-engineering reasoning and mitigation review; keep practical work within local challenge binaries.
phase_routing.P08: Use Sonnet for QEMU/Renode and firmware workflow implementation; Opus for boot-chain reasoning and cross-layer architecture; Fable may advise on ambitious non-sensitive hardware/software design. Record emulation limits.
phase_routing.P09: Use Haiku/Sonnet for synthetic test execution and result normalization; Opus for evaluation design and review. Mythos is optional only with verified program access; Fable safeguards may block cybersecurity tasks and must not be circumvented.
phase_routing.P10: Use Opus for system integration planning and cross-layer synthesis; Sonnet for implementation; Haiku for repetitive reporting; use an independent Opus or distinct model run to challenge critical findings. Fable may act as a high-level advisor where permitted.

effort_policy.low_or_medium: Routine, bounded, well-specified tasks; conserve context and usage.
effort_policy.high: Default for difficult reasoning and important review where supported.
effort_policy.xhigh: Reserve for long-running coding or agentic tasks on supported Opus 4.7+ models; use only when the expected value justifies the cost.
effort_policy.max: Rarely use for the most demanding analysis; do not make it the default.
effort_policy.rule: Use the model's supported effort settings and its current recommended default. Availability varies by model, product surface and account.

review_policy.critical_findings: Require a separate reviewer run with independent context; prefer a distinct model or model version when available.
review_policy.human_authority: Human approval remains required for scope changes, consequential execution, final vulnerability severity and external disclosure.
review_policy.correlated_error_warning: Multiple agents using the same model, prompt and evidence are not independent corroboration. Record model identity and independence assumptions.

runtime_discovery.policy: Discover available model IDs at runtime. Do not assume a model is enabled for every account, plan or organization.
runtime_discovery.pinning: Record the exact model ID, effort level and date for each run. Pin versions for benchmark comparisons; update defaults only through reviewed configuration changes.
runtime_discovery.fallback: If a preferred model is unavailable, select an available model by capability tier, rerun the applicable evaluation and record the substitution. Never silently downgrade a high-consequence review.

phase_transition_requires: Human or authorized curriculum controller approves transition
curriculum_control.failed_gate_behavior: Do not advance automatically. Identify the failed criterion, expose only the remediation brief for that criterion, and reassess after new evidence is produced.
curriculum_control.exception_behavior: A human may approve a skipped or modified gate. Record rationale, compensating evidence and residual risk. Never silently mark a gate passed.
curriculum_control.adaptation: The curriculum may adjust pacing and project difficulty based on demonstrated competency, but must preserve prerequisites, authorization controls and evidence standards.

knowledge_state_types.Observation: Directly recorded behaviour or source fact, linked to raw evidence.
knowledge_state_types.Hypothesis: A proposed explanation or possible weakness requiring further testing.
knowledge_state_types.Finding: A reviewed conclusion with evidence, affected scope, impact rationale and verification state.

edge_attributes.confidence: 0.0 to 1.0 with method and author recorded
edge_attributes.independent_observation_count: Integer count of genuinely independent observations
edge_attributes.impact: Separate severity or consequence field; never conflate with confidence

graph_rules: Never store secrets, credentials or private keys in Memgraph.
Store raw files in the artifact store and references/hashes in the graph.
Model-generated statements are not independent evidence.
Multiple agents sharing the same model, context and evidence are not automatically independent corroboration.
Confidence, severity, recency and reproducibility are distinct dimensions.
Every confirmed finding must link to supporting evidence and a review record.

evidence_contract.artifact_integrity: SHA-256 or a stronger reviewed content hash; preserve original bytes where lawful and authorized.
evidence_contract.reproducibility: Record environment, inputs, exact target version, tool versions and steps sufficient for an independent researcher to repeat the experiment.
evidence_contract.retention: Retain evidence according to project policy and applicable law; redact sensitive data before indexing or sharing.

evaluation.benchmark_design: Use fixed, versioned test cases containing seeded positive examples, benign decoys, incomplete evidence, contradictory evidence and synthetic prompt/tool injection cases.
evaluation.interpretation: Targets are internal engineering goals, not externally validated industry benchmarks. Report sample size and confidence intervals where meaningful.
hard_failures: Any fabricated evidence or falsely claimed tool success
Any confirmed finding without supporting provenance
evaluation.model_comparison: Compare models on the same target snapshot, test cases, tool versions, harness capabilities and effort settings. Report model and harness contributions separately.

completion_definition.core_outcome: A working research workbench that can accept an authorized mission, inspect a local software or emulated hardware target, run approved analysis, preserve immutable evidence, distinguish observations from hypotheses and confirmed findings, obtain independent review, and visualize provenance-rich relationships in Memgraph and Orb.
completion_definition.researcher_outcome: The researcher can independently explain system behaviour, evaluate candidate weaknesses, reproduce and root-cause controlled defects, validate mitigations and communicate limitations without relying on model authority.
completion_definition.not_claimed: Completion does not imply mastery of every security discipline, proof of physical hardware properties from emulation, or authorization to test external systems.

responsibilities: Capture exit status, raw output and artifacts
must_not: Accept direct agent authority as approval
Run arbitrary shell or network actions outside policy

independent_reviewer.purpose: Challenge evidence, reproduce claims where appropriate and identify unsupported conclusions.
responsibilities: Check reproducibility, impact rationale and remediation
must_not: Rely solely on the originating agent's summary
Silently rewrite the original evidence

evidence_curator.purpose: Preserve immutable artifacts and complete provenance records.
responsibilities: Link artifacts to missions, runs and observations
must_not: Alter original artifacts
Store secrets in the evidence index or graph

graph_steward.purpose: Maintain the Memgraph schema and ensure relationships are meaningful, sourced and queryable.
responsibilities: Preserve confidence, severity and recency as separate fields
Manage ingestion and graph quality checks
must_not: Create unsupported relationships
Convert agent repetition into independent evidence

harness_engineer.purpose: Maintain Claude Code integration and portable adapters without coupling the research core to one harness.
responsibilities: Maintain skills, hooks, agent definitions and adapters
Keep policy and evidence functions in the core
must_not: Treat harness prompts as the only security boundary
Hardcode unavailable model IDs

policy_engine.purpose: Apply deterministic authorization, scope and execution rules outside the model.
must_not: Infer authorization from user intent alone when a scope receipt is required
Allow agents to alter policy state

Mission.notes: Defines the authorized task and boundaries. It is not itself proof that every proposed operation is permitted.

ToolRequest.notes: A proposal submitted to the tool broker. The policy engine supplies the final decision; agents cannot set an allow decision.

AgentRun.notes: Captures model and harness provenance so results can be reproduced and compared.

Observation.notes: Records what was directly observed or derived. It is not automatically a vulnerability.

Hypothesis.notes: An explanation requiring further testing. Preserve contradictory evidence and unresolved status.

Finding.notes: A reviewed security conclusion. Confirmation requires evidence and independent review; a model score alone is insufficient.

Artifact.notes: Immutable original or derived research file. Preserve raw and transformed artifacts separately.

Review.notes: Records reviewer independence, evidence examined and any disagreement.

PhaseTransition.notes: Controls curriculum progression. A transition does not grant new target authorization.

agent_context_contract.output_rule: All outputs must conform to the task's declared schema. Missing data must be null, unknown or explicitly omitted according to the schema; never fabricate values.
agent_context_contract.memory_rule: Persist concise state summaries and artifact references. Do not treat chat history as the canonical research record.
